$comment: The contract between the React Native screens and the Xcode UI test (plan 3.4).
An XCUI test can only tap what it can address, and in React Native that
means a `testID`. If an identifier is renamed or dropped here, the UI test
does not fail loudly — it times out on an element that is no longer there,
or worse, it is never written because nobody knows what to query.
`scripts/quality/ui-test-ids.mjs` checks BOTH directions: every id below
must exist in the source, and every `testID` in the source must be listed
here. Only the identifiers the Login -> Task -> Photo -> Submit flow needs
are listed; add one when the UI test needs to touch something new.

ids.why: the worker types the store code here before signing in
the deployment's enrolment second factor, typed once on first installation
always present, so the test can tell 'still looking for a fix' from 'the screen is gone'
the way out of a refused or failed location lookup
disabled until a real GPS fix exists, so the test must wait for it
the rejection path (wrong store code, out of geofence)
the test taps the first task to open it
disabled until the checklist is complete, so the test must wait
the camera refuses to open until permission is granted, and this is how it is granted
lights the shelf — a general-trade outlet is often lit by one bulb
frames the shelf; steps through fractions of the device's maximum zoom
the planogram reference drawn over the live preview — the thing ghost_overlay_used claims
the running tally of barcodes decoded by expo-camera while the preview is live; lets the worker see the shelf is being read before the shutter
the photo the worker reviews before sending it
